result.topic_en: Derivation of Bradley's theory of astronomical refraction, assuming refractive index varies as a power of distance from Earth's centre, leading to formulas relating zenith distance, refraction and horizontal refraction.
result.transcription:
55.
Bradleys Refractionstheorie

Brechungsverhältnisse vom leeren Raume in die erste Schicht $1:M'$
zweite Schicht $1:M''$
dritte Schicht $1:M'''$ &c.

Einfallswinkel $I, I', I''$ etc., Abstände vom Mittelpuncte der Erde $R, R', R''$ &c.
Dann ist
$R\sin I = \frac{R'\sin I'}{M'} = \frac{R''\sin I''}{M''} = \frac{R'''\sin I'''}{M'''}$ &c. $= \frac{r\sin i}{m}$
Winkel am Mittelpuncte der Erde $= v$, so ist
$\frac{r\,dv}{dr} = \tan i = \frac{\mathfrak{R}m\sin I}{\sqrt{(rr - RRmm\sin I^2)}}$
Ist $m = \frac{r^\mu}{R^\mu}$ so ist $r^{1-\mu}$ [-$R$-] $\sin i = R^{1-\mu}\sin I$ also $\frac{(1-\mu)dr}{r} + \cot i\, di = 0$
$dv = -\frac{di}{1-\mu}$, $v = \mathrm{Const.} - \frac{i}{1-\mu}$
Letzte Werthe von $i, m, r$ ..... $Z, \mathfrak{M}, \mathfrak{R}$
$0 = \mathrm{Const} - \frac{Z}{1-\mu}$ also $i = Z - (1-\mu)v$. Letzter Werth von $v$ .... $V$
$I = Z - (1-\mu)V$. Nun ist $V + I = Z + \varrho$ also
$I = Z - \frac{1-\mu}{\mu}\varrho$, $R\sin(Z - \frac{1-\mu}{\mu}\varrho) = \frac{\mathfrak{R}\sin Z}{\mathfrak{M}}$ ; $\sin(Z - \frac{1-\mu}{\mu}\varrho) = \left(\frac{\mathfrak{R}}{R}\right)^{1-\mu}\sin Z$
$\frac{1-\mu}{\mu} = 2n$, Horizontalrefraction $= h$
1 $\sin(Z - 2n\varrho) = \cos 2nh . \sin Z$
2 $\sin n\varrho . \cos(Z - n\varrho) = \sin nh^2 . \sin Z$
3 $\cos n\varrho . \sin(Z - n\varrho) = \cos nh^2 . \sin Z$
$\tan n\varrho = \tan nh^2 \tan(Z - n\varrho)$
Hieraus, $\tan n\varrho = t$, $\tan nh = T$ gesetzt
$\tan Z = \frac{2tT}{TT - tt} . \frac{1+TT}{2T}$
oder
$\frac{2tT}{TT - tt} = \tan Z . \sin 2nh$
4 Es sei $\cos Z = \cos(Z - 2n\varrho)$ [-$\cos$-] $y$
so ist $\frac{\cos Z^2}{[-\cos-] y^2} + \sin Z^2 \cos 2nh^2 = 1 = \cos Z^2 + \sin Z^2$ also
$\cos Z^2$ [-$\cot$-] $\mathrm{tg}\, y^2 = \sin Z^2 \sin 2nh^2$
$\mathrm{tg}\, y = $ [-$\mathrm{tg}$-] $Z . \sin 2nh$
5. $\cos(Z - 2n\varrho)\sin\frac{1}{2}y^2 = \sin n\varrho \sin Z - n\varrho$
6. $\cos(Z - 2n\varrho)\cos\frac{1}{2}y^2 = \cos n\varrho \cos Z - n\varrho$
Aus 2.3.5.6.4.4
$\mathrm{tg}\, y^2 = \mathrm{tg}\, Z^2 \sin 2nh^2$
Aus $\frac{5}{6}.\frac{3}{2}$ $\mathrm{tg}\frac{1}{2}y^2\, \mathrm{tg}\, nh^2 = \mathrm{tg}\, n\varrho^2$

methods.what: Snell's law for spherically stratified atmosphere (invariant r sin i / m)
Differential equation of the ray path in polar coordinates
Power-law refractive index model m = (r/R)^mu and its integration
Bradley's refraction formula relating refraction to zenith distance
Refraction expressed via horizontal refraction h
Tangent form of the refraction law
Solution for tan Z in terms of t = tan n rho, T = tan nh
Auxiliary angle y method for computing refraction
